content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1 (as on 29.12.2025)
Key Insights

1. Rabi Sowing Status: As on December 26, 2025, the area sown under Rabi crops is 614.30 lakh ha (including 87.80 lakh ha in Rapeseed & Mustard & 95.88 lakh ha in Gram) as compared to 607.43 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  As on 26.12.2025, 98.50% of area has been harvested for Kharif crops all over India. Approximately, 65% area of Pulses mainly in Uradbean (100%), Moongbean (100%) & Mothbean (100%); 97.99% area of Oilseeds majorly in Groundnut (99.80%), Soyabean (100%)& Sesamum (99.78%); 97.24% area of Shri Anna cum Coarse Cereals, majorly in Jowar (98.47%) & Bajra (98.84%) and 98% area of Rice has been harvested for crops of Kharif 2025-26. 2. Weather Update:
a) Temperature: Minimum temperatures are likely to be above normal in NW India, Gujarat,

Bihar and NE India. Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal in East India, Central India, Maharashtra and South India. b) Rainfall Distribution: From October 01– December 28 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 12% higher than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-)1%; (ii) Northwest India: 25%; (iii) Central India: 35%; and South Peninsula: 4%.  A fresh Western Disturbance is likely to impact Western Himalayan Region from 30th December and adjoining Plains from 31st December, 2025.  Scattered to fairly widespread light/moderate rainfall/snowfall very likely over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit Baltistan-Muzaffarabad during 30th December-02nd January.  Isolated light/moderate rainfall/snowfall very likely over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh- Gilgit-Baltistan-Muzaffarabad on 29th Dec. Isolated light to moderate rainfall likely over Punjab, Haryana-Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh west Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Rajasthan 31st Dec to 01st Jan.  Isolated Thunderstorm and lightning with gusty wind likely to prevail over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 29th -31st December and 1st Jan.  Isolated to Scattered rainfall activity over Western Himalayan Region, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Islands.  Dense to very dense fog conditions very likely to continue during night/morning hours over Himachal Pradesh till 31st Dec; Punjab, Haryana-Chandigarh, west Uttar Pradesh till 31st December and east Uttar Pradesh till 01st Jan and reduction thereafter.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2 3. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 26 December 2025, the total live water storage in 166 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 147.04 billion cubic meter, which is 80.1% of total live storage capacity (183.565 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 106.78 percent of last year's storage and 123.25 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: In August 2025, around 89% of the country's monitoring stations exhibited a depth to water level within 10 meters below ground level. Deeper water levels of more than 20 m are observed in around 5% of stations of the country covering mainly the western states, especially Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.  The deeper groundwater level in the states like Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh during August 2025 has been significantly influenced by the over extraction of groundwater compared to the recharge during the monsoon period.  Annual water level comparison with the previous year August 2024 to August 2025 has shown that about 56.5% of total analyzed stations of the country experienced rise in annual water level fluctuation because of the higher rainfall in 2025 compared to 2024 in Monsoon period.  About 70% of the analyzed stations of the unconfined aquifer experienced a rise of water level in the decadal mean water level fluctuation of 2015-2024 with respect to August 2025. c) Fertilizers:. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 4. Pests & Diseases: There is no major pest incidence that has been reported. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 4
Details of each Segment
1. RAINFALL

 During the week (18 Dec – 24 Dec 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 65%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01st Oct to 24 Dec 2025) is higher than LPA by 14%. Rainfall Forecast:  Overall, rainfall activity is likely to be below over the country except Western Himalayan Region and northwest plains, where it is likely to be near normal to above normal.
2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX

Temerature Week 1 (26 Dec 2025 – 01 Jan 2026):  Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except northeast India & Western Himalayan Region and many parts of northwest India, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week.

5. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

Soil Moisture Observation  Soil moisture during 18 Dec – 24 Dec is similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of M.P, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Haryana, Punjab, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Telangana, A.P. and Bihar.  It was lower than average of past 9 years in pockets of Odisha, West Bengal and N.E. part of the country.
